decisions.statement: An affinity is shown once gained, being knowledge its holder has earned.
An affinity is shown as its name and the bare count it holds.
The cap an affinity's count fills toward is not shown beside that count.
No number behind an affinity is shown, neither its bias nor its cost nor its backlash.
A skill is shown as its rung and the level it holds within that rung.
What a gain felt like belongs to the prose rather than to this panel.
A slot with nothing in it is not shown, so gear not yet owned is not foretold.
The titles are not shown at all until the first title lands.
A part of the sheet already opened says it holds none yet rather than going away.
An affinity's tier is fused into its name, so no reader can tell a promotion apart.

definition: what a character is made of, as the play has left it
